chunks: And Fadala narrated from Aban, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAbdillah, who said: he said:
'Do not place hanoot in the ears of the deceased.'

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: al-mayyit — the deceased, the dead person
key_terms.حَنُوطًا: hanoot — fragrant camphor-based preparation applied to the deceased during the shrouding ritual (takhfīn)
key_terms.مَسَامِعِ: masāmiʿ — ear openings, the auditory passages of the deceased (pl. of masmāʿ)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia jurisprudence to place hanoot in the ears of the deceased during funeral preparation?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Fadala from Aban from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAbdillah, conveys a ruling attributed to one of the Imams (AS) — most likely Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — prohibiting the placement of hanoot (the fragrant camphor-based preparation used in ritual funeral preparation) in the ear openings (masāmiʿ) of the deceased. The double qāla indicates ʿAbd al-Rahman is directly quoting the Imam's pronouncement. This narration sits within the broader jurisprudential discussion delimiting the seven prostration points as the correct sites for hanoot application, and rules out the ears as a permissible site.
